solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Whip-round for depressed area in the countryside

blocks.note: a riding crop is a short whip
a round shape is a circle

explanation.surface: A village collection is taken for some sunken patch of rural land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip-round' looks like one word for a collection of money, but it splits into two synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop circle is a flattened pattern in a field, so it is literally a pressed-down patch of farmland.

clue.text: One often hailed monarch once as icon of the Highlands

blocks.note: a taxi is often hailed in the street
Elizabeth Regina, the late queen

explanation.surface: A former king was cheered as a symbol of the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hailed' suggests acclaimed, but it is hailing a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: Tossing the caber, a long tree trunk, is the emblematic event of Scottish Highland games.

clue.text: Want to drop page journalist replaced when editing?

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: want is lack, poverty
P is the abbreviation for page
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper wants to axe a page and swap in another reporter at the editing stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' is the noun meaning need or lack, not the verb; ED, for editor, is the usual crossword journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtyped text has had new characters typed over it, replacing what was there during editing.

clue.text: Money, after reflecting, no object after cardplayers have a rethink

indicators.note: something reflected in a mirror is seen backwards
after places the following piece behind the cardplayers in the final order

blocks.note: loose coins are change
taken as written
East and South are partners at bridge
to object is to mind

explanation.surface: Bridge players, having pondered, decide money is no obstacle and rethink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money no object' reads as a set phrase but splits into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To change one's mind is to reconsider and reach a different decision.

clue.text: Mean to turn to drink a lot: it's on the house!

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the other way
to drink something is to take it inside you

blocks.note: poor quality is mean
doing something a lot is doing it often, oft

explanation.surface: A stingy man takes up heavy drinking because the bar is serving free rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: ROOP takes OFT inside it. 'On the house' sounds like free drinks; read literally, it is where the definition sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooftop is literally the top surface of a house, so it is on the house.

clue.text: Short of people — not ministers — to embrace the Tories

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside the arms, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: laic means of the laity, not the clergy
Con is short for Conservative

explanation.surface: Lacking voters who are not in government, so needing Conservative support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ministers' are church ministers, not government ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech is terse and brief, so short in what it says.

clue.text: Pinched stuff from comedian going on second

indicators.note: in an across clue, one item going on another is placed after it

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
a wag is a joker or wit

explanation.surface: Stolen goods are traced to a stand-up comic who comes on second in the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Swag is slang for loot, the goods a burglar has stolen.

clue.text: Without trio to follow cue you can hear, defeat

blocks.note: w/o is the written abbreviation for without

blocks.clueFragment: trio to follow cue you can hear
blocks.note: cue sounds like the letter Q, and the three letters after Q in the alphabet come next

explanation.surface: A snooker player cannot cope without three shots to follow the cue.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone only names the letter Q to count from; Q itself is not in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To worst an opponent is to get the better of them, to defeat them.

clue.text: Rodent with reason to keep to itself

blocks.note: grounds for something are reasons
to hog is to keep selfishly

explanation.surface: A solitary rodent has good reason to avoid company.
explanation.definitionFit: The groundhog, or woodchuck, is a North American marmot, a burrowing rodent.

clue.text: Put up with black stuff in one part of leg

indicators.note: to stuff is to pack something inside another thing

blocks.note: taken as written
to put up a candidate is to nominate them
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates dark material inside one section of a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' looks like tolerate, but 'with' just joins B on; NOMINATE plus B is stuffed into IN ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The innominate bone is the hip bone, joining the leg to the trunk, so loosely a part of the leg.

clue.text: Buzzer a girl presses makes one cross

indicators.note: to press something is to hold it close in an embrace, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: a bee is an insect that buzzes
Flo is a short girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl pushes a doorbell, which makes somebody angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the adjective angry, but it is a noun for a hybrid animal; 'presses' means hugs, not pushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A beefalo is a hybrid bred from domestic cattle and the American bison, so it is a crossbreed.

clue.text: Lively do with brandy to start, then port

indicators.note: to start means only the opening letter of the word before it is wanted

blocks.note: to do someone is to swindle or con them
first letter of brandy
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A lively party serves brandy first and port afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' reads as a noun for a party, but it is the verb meaning cheat. 'Port' is a city, not the fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Con brio is a musical direction meaning play with vigour and spirit.

clue.text: Tense over tethering stray

indicators.note: to stray is to wander from the proper place, so these letters move out of order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frets about tying up an animal that has wandered off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective for anxious; with 'over' it is the verb meaning make taut again.
explanation.definitionFit: To tense something over is to tauten it a second time, which is what retighten means.

clue.text: Decide to join switch components in metal work

indicators.note: switching the parts tells you the two words of the phrase that follows swap places

blocks.note: OP is short for opus, a work
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A workman installs electrical switch parts in a piece of metalwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metal work' gives TIN then OP; switching those two components puts OP first.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt in is to choose to take part in a scheme, that is to elect to join.

clue.text: Not an ounce lighter

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for nothing at all
second meaning: a well-known brand of petrol cigarette lighter

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests something weighing less than an ounce; 'lighter' is really a noun, the device for lighting cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Zippo is informal for zero, and Zippo is also the trade name of a refillable metal lighter.

clue.text: An element of unknown in our mic malfunctioning

indicators.note: a malfunctioning device is not working properly, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: z is an algebraic unknown
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Part of something mysterious inside our faulty microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Zirconium is a chemical element, a grey metal with atomic number 40.

clue.text: Film-maker's expression of disgust after endless kissing

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off the word that follows
after places the expression behind the other piece in the final order

blocks.note: a peck is a light kiss
pah is an exclamation of contempt

explanation.surface: A director scoffs after a kiss is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: A peck is a quick light kiss, so kissing becomes pecking before it is shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam Peckinpah was an American director known for violent westerns such as The Wild Bunch.

clue.text: Maybe sticks kinky Rose in PVC

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so these letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman called Rose dressed in shiny plastic gear may stick around.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The sticks' is slang for remote rural areas, and the provinces are the regions away from the capital.

clue.text: Reactionary getting drunk on wine

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another comes after it

blocks.note: red is a colour of wine
to neck a drink is to down it quickly

explanation.surface: A die-hard conservative gets tipsy on wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like intoxicated, but it is the past tense of drink, matching the slang verb neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Rednecked describes the bigoted, ultra-conservative attitudes associated with the stereotype of a redneck.

clue.text: Loud party in joint, with drink

blocks.note: the knee is a joint
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A noisy party takes place in a seedy bar where people drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests a dive or bar, but it is a body joint. A knees-up is British slang for a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: A knees-up is informal British for a boisterous party with dancing.

clue.text: Figure no longer living in the past, note

blocks.note: dec. is the abbreviation for deceased
ago means in the past
N is short for note

explanation.surface: A historical figure, long dead, is noted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests a person, but it is a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A decagon is a plane figure with ten sides.

clue.text: Piece taken dal segno maestro turned in

indicators.note: a piece taken from the following words means a run of letters is lifted from them
turned means the lifted letters face the other way round

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling segno and maestro

explanation.surface: A musician plays a passage from the sign, as the conductor turned to it.
explanation.walkthrough: Dal segno is a musical instruction to repeat from the sign; the letters GNOMA read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Among and in are prepositions both meaning placed within a group, as in 'among friends'.

clue.text: Second of concerts by celebrity, mainly for charity

indicators.note: the second of a word means just its second letter is used
mainly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: second letter of concerts
x means by in multiplication, as in three by four
celebrity is fame

explanation.surface: A star plays a second concert, mostly to raise money for a good cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxfam is a major British-founded charity working against global poverty.

clue.text: Vestment from back of shelf with no name tag

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: last letter of shelf
anon. stands for anonymous, bearing no name

explanation.surface: A robe taken down from a shelf has lost its label.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanon is a liturgical vestment, a cape-like garment worn by the Pope.

clue.text: Avoiding key work by sculptor?

blocks.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
a sculptor hews stone, cutting it into shape

explanation.surface: Someone sidesteps the main piece of a sculptor's output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' suggests a musical key or something important, but it is the computer key. The question mark flags that hewing is just one sort of work a sculptor might do.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to shun or abstain from it, so eschewing is avoiding.

clue.text: Complaint spread from mouth to ear

indicators.note: passing from one person's mouth to another's ear is speech that is listened to

blocks.note: something that has spread has grown

explanation.surface: A grievance passes by word of mouth from one person to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' as a past participle means grown; the sound of grown gives a word spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A groan can be a grumble or complaint, as in 'moans and groans'.

clue.text: For which there's prize money after dismissing opener?

definitions.text: For which there's prize money after dismissing opener?

indicators.note: dismissing the opener means the first letter is sent away

blocks.note: money won is winnings

explanation.surface: A cricket question: what is the prize for getting the opening batsman out?
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the first letter of WINNINGS. Read whole, the clue describes a cricket team's turn at the crease, which begins after an opening batsman (opener) is out, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an innings is a batting turn, and the wordplay's cricket language of opener and dismissal paints that turn.

clue.text: Hugo or Charlie's eccentric comic brother

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Choosing between two men, Hugo or Charlie, for the oddball funny sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho was one of the Marx Brothers, the American comedy siblings.

clue.text: A lot of a certain breed of cat, appropriately, unknown

indicators.note: this cat breed is famous for having no tail, so appropriately its word loses its tail too

blocks.note: the Manx is a cat breed from the Isle of Man
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A great many cats of a particular breed are of unknown origin.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manx cat is naturally tailless, so its name drops its last letter to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Many' replaces 'a lot of' before a plural noun: many cats, a lot of cats.

clue.text: When nothing is restricting, as one's slaughtered?

definitions.text: When nothing is restricting, as one's slaughtered?

indicators.note: slaughtered means hacked about, so these letters are mangled into a new order

blocks.note: O is zero, nothing
someone who pens animals is restricting them
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about the time when no rule protects game, so anything may be shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'one' is just has, as in 'one has been slaughtered'. Read whole, the clue describes a period when hunting is unrestricted.
explanation.definitionFit: Open season is the part of the year when the legal ban on hunting a species is lifted.
